patterns.usage_note: Marks the place or state something separates from, with intransitive verbs of departure and exit (出る、降りる、離れる), plus 卒業する. Nothing is acted on here, so it behaves quite unlike the direct-object を: the noun is simply the point left behind. から is often available with the motion verbs (家を出る／家から出る, バスを降りる／バスから降りる), where を frames the departure as one completed event and から draws attention to the physical path out; but with 卒業する only を works (○大学を卒業する, ×大学から卒業する).

examples.ruby: 兄[あに]は毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]に家[いえ]を出[で]て走[はし]っている。
examples.english: My brother leaves the house at six every morning and goes running.

examples.ruby: 次[つぎ]の角[かど]でバスを降[お]りたほうが近道[ちかみち]だよ。
examples.english: You're better off getting off the bus at the next corner; it's a shortcut.

examples.ruby: 姉[あね]は去年[きょねん]大学[だいがく]を卒業[そつぎょう]して働[はたら]いている。
examples.english: My sister graduated from university last year and is working now.
